findings.observation: The long metallic surface is a narrow horizontal rail with three very thin visible legs and no joined side return, substantial apron or readable top plane. A second long rail lies much lower in the foreground with no visible support or side connection to the first. In both the served full room and populated native cases it reads as an open barrier/bench assembly, not a coherent gaming counter surface.
findings.qualification: Three legs ARE present. This is not a claim that all support pixels are absent; the failures are the disconnected assembly and inadequate mass/depth at actual play scale.

findings.observation: Moving floor highlights paint over static support material rather than remaining behind it, weakening the support/floor depth separation.

The enclosure does not show a convincing lower booth/counter mass or side thickness; the machine stack also lacks a continuous supported work surface. findings.observation: The full-width reddish wood strip has a nearly straight upper and lower boundary and repeated slanted divisions. It reads as a steep wall/ramp or barrier, not a receding pier/deck top. It separates bright upper sand from dark lower ground without a visible connecting ramp, steps or coherent continuous walking plane. Bonfire benches/windbreak, storm rentals/skiff/Stranger, and festival rope/exit stand over the wood face rather than on an unambiguous horizontal floor.
findings.consequence: The actual populated views expose a ground/prop registration failure that empty source art and object-count/occlusion checks did not resolve.

findings.observation: The umbrella canopy is an almost frontal triangular motif at the upper sand edge. Its bright narrow pole descends into the wooden face and ends there, with no legible planted foot or cast shadow on a horizontal plane. A bonfire bench and storm closing stall sit underneath/alongside the same face, reinforcing the contradictory depth.
findings.next_visual_requirement: Canopy underside/top foreshortening, visible pole-to-ground contact and one shadow direction must agree with the repaired deck plane and unchanged nearby population anchors.

findings.observation: Long repeated magenta/cyan bars float across the dark sky with no poles, cable, awning or truss. They read as an indoor ceiling-light row. Their repeated scale and flat alignment, together with near-uniform sea strip texture, weaken outdoor horizon depth instead of establishing distance.
findings.uncertainty: They could be intended decorative lights, but the actual source contains no supporting structure. A support/rehome/removal choice is an owner composition decision, not approved by this report.

findings.observation: The sea is a broad repeated horizontal strip with little texture-scale falloff. In Storm, the upright late-swimmer portrait is fully drawn above the water with a dry-style base shadow, and the lifeguard stands at the upper sand edge; the current background does not clearly explain these depth anchors. The slot cabinet over the towel fascia also lacks a legible grounded counter body/side return.
findings.qualification: Swimming/wading or a raised kiosk can be intentional. Do not move these gameplay anchors to force a prettier image. The corrected art must explain the existing positions, or expose an explicit anchor/design conflict for owner review first.

next_bounded_correction: First prepare a single non-active ground/pier composition registered to the full existing four-context anchor envelope. Decide which band is sand, deck top and deck front; create one believable receding top plane, side/underside and sand-to-deck connection. Keep every gameplay object position, route, hit region and scenario definition unchanged.

Within that ground trial, redraw the umbrella at the same approved anchor with a coherent canopy/pole/foot shadow and give the towel/slot counter a grounded body. Do not generate or accept a whole-room replacement from an empty render.

Then resolve sky lights and sea-distance cues against that same perspective. Preserve all surf/boat/sign/glint identities and animation timing/liveness; no suppression or pointer-triggered redraw workaround.
